## The tools RPC

`boxd.machines.tools` is the family's v2 module, copied verbatim outside its plugin block: a script calls each tool with
no model, as a session and its agent. The rules decide: only a resolved `allow` runs, an `ask` is refused because no one
can answer it, and every change still asserts inside its own run.

# Configuration

## Options

All options go in the plugin entry in `opencode.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{
    "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-boxd#v0.0.4",
    "options": { "snapshot": "opencode-golden" }
  }]
}
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot` | `opencode-golden` | The golden snapshot every new machine boots from. A lowercase boxd snapshot name. Build it as [golden-image.md](golden-image.md) describes. |
| `allowUntestedHost` | `false` | Run on an OpenCode outside `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`. Status then says the host is untested. |
| `allowedRoots` | `[]` | Absolute laptop folders a work may read and write besides the project. A path outside both is refused. |
| `access` | `"all"` | What the plugin's own tools may do without asking: `"all"` allows everything, `"ask-changes"` allows the reads and asks for every machine change, `"read-only"` allows the reads and denies every change. A later rule of the user's still wins. |

An unknown option, a snapshot name boxd would refuse, or a non-boolean `allowUntestedHost` stops the plugin with
`OPTIONS_INVALID`; OpenCode's plugin list shows why.

Inside `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0` a release that was not tested, such as 2.2.99, still starts: status marks the version `untested`
and the next step is the same as on a tested release. Outside the range the plugin does not start unless
`allowUntestedHost` is `true`.

## Where the ledger lives

`~/.local/share/opencode-boxd/works/<work id>/`

- `work.json` — the machine, the laptop folder and the guest work folder, the root session id, the proof, the git record,
  and the files moved in and out by name, size and sha256.
- `exports/<session id>.json` — the transcript, stored before it is imported here.
- `patch.diff` — the uncommitted diff, when the harvest found one.
- `untracked.json` — the untracked files' contents, base64, when the harvest could read them.

The ledger is the laptop's copy. A boxd snapshot is an image and holds no session you can restore from the laptop.

## Permission rules

The plugin inserts its block directly after each agent's base `* * allow`. The last matching rule wins, so a rule of
yours later in the agent, or in the session, still decides.

The block is generated from `defaultRules(access)`, and it is printed here in full for each value, so it can be copied
into an agent that gets no block of its own.

`access: "all"` (the default):

```json
[
  {"action":"boxd_*","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_status","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_job","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_ensure","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_submit","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_harvest","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_sleep","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_resume","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_image","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_drop","resource":"*","effect":"allow"}
]
```

`access: "ask-changes"`:

```json
[
  {"action":"boxd_*","resource":"*","effect":"ask"},
  {"action":"boxd_status","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_job","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_ensure","resource":"*","effect":"ask"},
  {"action":"boxd_submit","resource":"*","effect":"ask"},
  {"action":"boxd_harvest","resource":"*","effect":"ask"},
  {"action":"boxd_sleep","resource":"*","effect":"ask"},
  {"action":"boxd_resume","resource":"*","effect":"ask"},
  {"action":"boxd_image","resource":"*","effect":"ask"},
  {"action":"boxd_drop","resource":"*","effect":"ask"}
]
```

`access: "read-only"`:

```json
[
  {"action":"boxd_*","resource":"*","effect":"deny"},
  {"action":"boxd_status","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_job","resource":"*","effect":"allow"},
  {"action":"boxd_ensure","resource":"*","effect":"deny"},
  {"action":"boxd_submit","resource":"*","effect":"deny"},
  {"action":"boxd_harvest","resource":"*","effect":"deny"},
  {"action":"boxd_sleep","resource":"*","effect":"deny"},
  {"action":"boxd_resume","resource":"*","effect":"deny"},
  {"action":"boxd_image","resource":"*","effect":"deny"},
  {"action":"boxd_drop","resource":"*","effect":"deny"}
]
```

Every tool this plugin registers is allowed by default, so an agent can create, run and destroy a billing machine
without a prompt. The guards that do not depend on a prompt still hold: a machine that idles hibernates, `boxd_sleep`
always works, drop refuses anything the laptop cannot account for, and the ledger records a create before it runs.

An agent without a base allow gets no rules: inserting there would turn a default deny into an ask. `/boxd-status` names
each agent that lacks the block, and prints the block for the access value in force to paste first in that agent's own
permissions, followed by your top-level rules for boxd tools.

## Platform facts

- **`opencode session import` keeps the transcript's id**, tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0. A second import of the same
  transcript answers `Session already exists` on stderr, exits 0, and prints no id; the plugin treats that as the
  transcript's own id. Tested against each stock release in `test/unit/prover.test.ts`.
- **The prover runs `opencode session import --standalone`**, so the import writes the same store whether or not a
  service is running, and never waits on one.
- **The guest must run the same OpenCode as the laptop.** The plugin reads `opencode --version` on the machine and
  compares it with the host's own version.
- **The snapshot is checked before a create.** `boxd_status` reads `boxd snapshots list --json` (cached for 30
  seconds) and says whether the image is there. `boxd_ensure` and `boxd_resume` read it again before creating a machine
  and refuse with `SNAPSHOT_MISSING`, so no machine boots from nothing. An unreadable listing is not a refusal: the
  create reports its own error.
- **Status reads, never wakes.** `boxd_status` runs one read-only `machine get` per open work and one `machine list`;
  `/boxd-status`, the `/boxd` dialog and the status RPC read the same. No read wakes a machine, because waking starts
  billing. The plugin never reads your boxd account or credentials: the `machine list` answer is how status says the
  boxd CLI is signed in (`cli.signedIn`), and a failed one keeps the CLI's reason, because a network failure fails the
  same way.
- **A read never wakes.** `boxd_job` reports `asleep` for a hibernated machine and names `boxd_resume` as the next step.
  `asleepBy` is `boxd_sleep` (with `sleptAt`) when the plugin hibernated it and has not woken it since, and
  `idle_or_cli` otherwise: the 30-minute idle bound, or the boxd CLI. boxd does not say when a machine hibernated by
  itself. Status shows the same per work. The plugin cannot see a wake it did not make: a machine woken outside it,
  by the boxd CLI or an SSH connection, and put down again by the idle bound still reports `boxd_sleep` with the older
  `sleptAt`, until the plugin wakes or recreates it.
- **Hibernating destroys nothing.** `boxd_sleep` needs no proof and works when the guest cannot be harvested; it records
  a warning that the last prompt is not on the laptop yet, which status shows. `boxd_image` and `boxd_drop` still need a
  fresh proof.
- **The guest path is the plugin's.** Every work's guest folder is `/home/boxd/work/<work id>`; the laptop folder is
  recorded beside it in the ledger. A laptop path is never sent to the guest, and a guest that cannot prepare its own
  folder fails with `GUEST_WORKSPACE` and the guest's own words.
- **Files carry name, size and digest.** An upload is copied before the prompt; a harvest copies the requested files
  back after the transcript. A file is refused outside the project and `allowedRoots`, over 8 MiB, over 32 MiB a call,
  through a symlink, or over a local edit since the last harvest. A copied-back file is written through a temp file and
  a rename, 0600, and the ledger records name, size and sha256, never content.
- **A run's outcome is part of the result.** OpenCode records it on the session (`outcome`) and on its last idle message,
  with the failure's structured error. `boxd_job` reports it when the guest is idle, `boxd_harvest` records it and adds
  `GUEST_RUN_FAILED` or `GUEST_AUTH_FAILED` as a warning, and status shows each work's last outcome. The error is `<type>: <first line>`, passed
  through redaction; a provider's response body is never read. It comes from the guest or the imported transcript, never
  from a model call.
- **A job says what the session last did.** On a running machine `boxd_job` adds `lastText` (the newest assistant text,
  redacted and cut to 300 characters), `lastActivityAt` and `pending` (prompts waiting in the session's inbox). Each is
  read from the guest's own session with no model call, and left out when the guest does not answer it.
- **Drop only destroys what the laptop can account for.** It refuses a non-git directory, untracked or ignored paths, and
  a dirty tree with no stored patch. Tracked changes are stored as `git diff HEAD`; untracked contents are stored beside
  it when the guest can read them, which is not the same as a faithful copy, so a drop still refuses.
- **A create is recorded before it runs.** The ledger holds the intent, so a timed-out `machine new` is either adopted
  when the machine appears, or reported as `CREATE_UNCERTAIN`, and `boxd_status` names an `oc-*` machine no work records.
- **Every wake arms the awake bound.** `machine config set auto-hibernate.timeout 1800` and `idle.ignore-outbound off`
  run right after a wake or create; a sleep sets the timeout to 14400.

## Errors

Every plugin error reads `CODE: What happened. Next step: What to do.`, with exactly one next step. A tool's result
for it is `{ "error": "<CODE>", "message": "<what happened>", "next": "<what to do>" }`, so a Code Mode program or a
script reads the same three parts the model does. Upstream and host
errors pass through unchanged. No error, log or status line contains a token, a code or a signed URL.

| Code | What it means |
|---|---|
| `HOST_UNTESTED` | OpenCode is outside `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0` and `allowUntestedHost` is not set. |
| `OPTIONS_INVALID` | The plugin options are not valid. |
| `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE` | The status RPC could not read the status. |
| `SKILLS_INVALID` | The plugin's skill file is missing or malformed. |
| `NAME_INVALID` | A work id, guest path, snapshot name or prompt is not in the form the plugin accepts. |
| `NOT_OURS` | No open work, or the machine is not the one the ledger records for it. |
| `MACHINE_GONE` | The machine no longer exists. `boxd_resume` rebuilds it. |
| `MACHINE_STARTING` | The machine or its OpenCode is not up yet. Nothing waits inside a call. |
| `MACHINE_SHARED` | The machine is shared, which deletes the guest's OpenCode sign-in. |
| `MACHINE_ISOLATED` | The machine is isolated, so it has no git and no in-VM boxd CLI. |
| `SESSION_BUSY` | The guest session is still running; harvest only when it is idle. |
| `GUEST_VERSION` | The machine's OpenCode differs from this laptop's. |
| `GUEST_RUN_FAILED` | The guest session's last run failed. The transcript is still imported and proven; the error is the run's own. |
| `RUN_INTERRUPTED` | The guest's OpenCode stopped during a run, so the run never finished. The transcript is kept. Call `boxd_harvest`, then `boxd_submit` again. |
| `GUEST_AUTH_FAILED` | The guest session's last run failed on a model credential. The transcript is still imported; fix the guest's sign-in. |
| `GUEST_FAILED` | The guest helper failed an action. |
| `GUEST_UNRESPONSIVE` | A guest call timed out, and a probe of the machine found under a tenth of its memory available, or a load over four per CPU. The message gives the free memory, the load and the three largest processes by name and pid. |
| `GUEST_SERVER_DOWN` | A guest call timed out, and a probe found the machine well but nothing listening on the OpenCode port. The next guest call starts the server again. |
| `BOXD_FAILED` | The boxd CLI refused a command or returned something unusable. |
| `BOXD_MISSING` | The boxd CLI is not on the `PATH`, or the one there is the in-VM CLI, which this plugin does not support. |
| `TIMEOUT` | A boxd command did not answer in time. After a guest call, a probe that found the machine well, server included, adds what it found. |
| `NOT_PROVEN` | No fresh laptop import. Sleep, image and drop refuse. |
| `DIRTY` | The guest tree has uncommitted work and no stored patch. |
| `EXPORT_INVALID` | An export is not in OpenCode's session shape. |
| `PARENT_MISSING` | A child session was imported before its parent. |
| `SNAPSHOT_EXISTS` | Snapshot names are immutable. |
| `SNAPSHOT_MISSING` | The golden snapshot is not in this boxd account, so no machine is created. |
| `LEDGER_FAILED` | A ledger read or write failed: a file system error, not a boxd one. |
| `RULES_NOT_ADDED` | The default permission rules could not be inserted into the agents, so a machine change may run without asking. |
| `UNTRACKED` | The guest tree has untracked or ignored paths, which a stored patch cannot hold. |
| `GIT_UNKNOWN` | The guest directory is not a git repository, so nothing about its files can be proven. |
| `CREATE_UNCERTAIN` | `machine new` timed out and no machine with that name exists yet. |
| `PATH_REFUSED` | A laptop path is outside the project and `allowedRoots`, or is a symlink. Name its root in the option, and allow it with the `external_directory` rule as well as the path rule. |
| `FILE_TOO_LARGE` | A file is over 8 MiB, or one call moves over 32 MiB. |
| `FILE_CONFLICT` | A harvested file was edited on the laptop since the last harvest. |
| `GUEST_WORKSPACE` | The guest could not create or prepare `/home/boxd/work/<work id>`. |

# The golden image

Every machine the plugin creates boots from one snapshot: the golden image. It must contain the OpenCode version this
laptop runs, and a way for the session to reach a model. It must not contain a credential of its own if you can avoid it.

The stock boxd image does **not** contain OpenCode 2: a stock machine ships 1.19.5, which is a 1.x release and ignores
the guest server's password. Build your own once, and set the plugin's `snapshot` option to its name.

The default name is `opencode-golden`. `boxd_status` says when it is missing, and `boxd_ensure` and `boxd_resume` refuse
to create a machine without it.

## 1. A machine to build it on

Make a private machine from the stock image and open a shell on it. Do this with the `boxd` CLI, outside the plugin:

```sh
boxd machine new golden-builder --label role=image --json
boxd machine connect golden-builder
```

There is no stock snapshot to name: omit `--from-snapshot`, and `machine get` then reports `source: standalone`.
`machine connect` gives a real login shell; `boxd machine exec golden-builder -- bash` does not, and interactive
commands such as `opencode auth login` exit silently under it.

Set a short idle bound while the machine waits for you, so it does not bill:

```sh
boxd machine config set golden-builder auto-hibernate.timeout 1800
```

Do not pass `--shared`: sharing deletes OpenCode's sign-in. Do not pass `--isolated`: the image keeps git and the in-VM
`boxd` CLI, which a session machine needs.

## 2. The OpenCode version that matches the laptop

The guest must run exactly the version on this laptop. Print it on the laptop first:

```sh
opencode --version        # for example: opencode v2.2.5
```

The guest ships 1.x, so upgrade across the major version first, then pin the laptop's exact release:

```sh
opencode upgrade --major  # installs the newest 2.x, for example 2.2.6
opencode upgrade 2.2.5    # the exact version the laptop runs
opencode --version        # must equal the laptop's, to the patch release
```

`opencode upgrade 2.2.5` from 1.x refuses with "OpenCode 2.2.5 is OpenCode 2"; the `--major` step is what makes 2.x
reachable. Both steps together take a few seconds.

Check that the server password works, because the guest helper depends on it. Check both directions and stop the
server afterwards:

```sh
OPENCODE_PASSWORD=probe opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096 &
sleep 5
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/info                 # 401, not 200
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -u opencode:probe http://127.0.0.1:4096/api/info # 200
pkill -f "opencode serve"
```

A `200` without credentials means the server ignored the password: the image holds a 1.x OpenCode, and every session on
it would be open to anything that can reach the port. Leaving the test server running puts it inside the snapshot.

## 3. A way to reach a model

The recommended path keeps **no credential in the image**. A boxd environment variable is injected into every machine
at boot, so the image can stay clean:

```sh
boxd env set --secret OPENCODE_API_KEY <key> --domain '*.opencode.ai,opencode.ai'
```

- `--secret` seals the value: `boxd env list` shows `(sealed)`, never the value.
- Bind it to the provider's hosts with `--domain`, so the guest cannot send it anywhere else.
- Scope it to the org (default `all`) or to you (`private`); either is injected at boot by `boxd-takeoff` into
  `/etc/profile.d/boxd-env.sh`.
- The machine boots with the variable already set, `auth.json` stays absent, and every image you build inherits the
  arrangement without holding the key.

Two things to know:

- A **Go Teams service-account** key does not work for model calls. The guest answers
  `provider.auth … Go Teams covers workspace members, not service accounts. Use a personal API key to call Go models.`
  Use a personal provider key with a **spending limit**.
- The injected variables are readable by anything on the machine and by anyone who can boot a machine in the
  organisation: they are injected at boot, not baked into the image, but every boot has them. Rotate the key if someone
  leaves.
- A short-lived token, such as a GitHub App installation token that lives one hour, must be set again before it
  expires. A refresh that runs on the laptop stops while the laptop sleeps, and every guest that pushes after that gets
  a 401. Tell a session in its prompt to stop and report a 401 or 403: it cannot finish an interactive sign-in, such as
  `boxd manage integrations connect git`, without a person.

### Signing in on the machine, as a fallback

If you cannot use `boxd env`, sign the guest's OpenCode in **on the machine itself**:

```sh
ssh -t golden-builder.boxd opencode auth login
```

`ssh -t` (or `boxd machine connect` then `opencode auth login`) is required: `boxd machine exec --tty … -- opencode auth
login` exits with no picker. Never copy `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` from the laptop, and never paste a token into
a prompt: an agent's transcript would hold it. Confirm without printing the secret:

```sh
ssh -t golden-builder.boxd opencode auth list
```

`auth list` already names providers that come from environment variables, so look for the provider you added with a
stored credential, not for a longer list.

A credential stored this way is on the image's disk. Anyone in the organisation who can boot the image inherits it: use a
dedicated key with a spending limit, and rotate it when someone leaves. This is why the environment path is preferred.

## 4. Remove the injected values before you save

`boxd-takeoff` writes the environment variables to `/etc/profile.d/boxd-env.sh` on the machine's disk. Delete that file
just before the snapshot, so the image carries no copy; it is regenerated from `boxd env` at the next boot:

```sh
sudo rm -f /etc/profile.d/boxd-env.sh
```

Clear any shell history too. Leave nothing else changed.

## 5. Save it

Nothing may be running that holds a session you care about, and the machine should be clean of scratch work.

```sh
boxd snapshots save golden-builder opencode-golden --json     # a few seconds for a ~10 GiB disk, an image either way
boxd snapshots list --json                                    # the name, status "ready", version 1
boxd machine remove golden-builder -y
```

Point the plugin at it in `opencode.json` (or rely on the default name):

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{
    "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-boxd#v0.0.4",
    "options": { "snapshot": "opencode-golden" }
  }]
}
```

`boxd_status` shows `Snapshot: opencode-golden (present)`. A name that is not there shows `(not in this boxd account)`,
with this doc as its next step.

## The disclosure

**A snapshot that holds model credentials can be booted by anyone in your boxd organisation who can see or use
snapshots.** A credential stored on the disk is inherited by every machine created from it. The environment path keeps
the value out of the image, but every boot still has it. Treat either arrangement as a shared secret:

- use a provider key made for the image, with a spending limit, and rotate it if anyone leaves the organisation;
- do not put personal tokens, mail credentials or a second provider on the image;
- delete an old image when you replace it (`boxd snapshots remove <name> -y`), so the old arrangement cannot be booted.

The plugin itself never copies credentials to or from a machine, and never reads your laptop's credential store.

## Rebuilding it when the laptop's OpenCode changes

`GUEST_VERSION` means the machine's OpenCode is not this laptop's, and `boxd_status` shows the version the guest must
have. When you upgrade OpenCode on the laptop:

1. build a new image as above, with the new version, and a new name, such as `opencode-golden-2.2.7`;
2. set `snapshot` to the new name;
3. run `boxd_resume` for each open work: a machine that is gone is rebuilt from the new image and its proven transcript;
4. delete the old image once no work needs it.

A snapshot is an image, not a session: rebuilding it never carries a transcript. The laptop's ledger does.

# Jelly

Jelly reads the `jelly` section of `package.json` to show this plugin in its marketplace and to decide
what a Jelly may call.

## What it declares

- **`tools`** — all nine, by their permission action, with the effect the default rules give: every one of them `allow`,
  the two reads and the seven machine changes alike. 9 tools are declared (2 read-only): `boxd_status` and `boxd_job`
  are the reads.
- **`skills`** — `boxd`.
- **`signIns`** — empty. The plugin has no sign-in of its own: it runs your `boxd` CLI, which you sign in to with
  `boxd auth login`, and Jelly cannot show that sign-in on the card. `/boxd-status` shows it as its first row, **boxd
  CLI**, with `boxd auth login` as the next step when the CLI does not answer.
- **`icon`** — `assets/icon.svg`, boxd's own mark: boxd.sh's `favicon.svg`, unchanged, on a rounded tile in boxd.sh's page colour #0a0c12 (`opencode.vendor.mark` is `true`).
- **`contributes`** — one setting, `access`, the option of the same name, as a choice of three: **Allowed** (`all`, the
  default), **Ask before changes** (`ask-changes`) and **Read only** (`read-only`), with Jelly's own line for each.
  Jelly draws it as a choice and saves only one of the three; a Jelly that does not know declared choices yet refuses
  the whole declaration. No home feed, widget or work kind.

Every tool the plugin registers is declared: the nine tools are the plugin's own, and `test/unit/jelly.test.ts` fails
when a tool in `src/tools.ts` is missing from `jelly.tools`, so a release cannot add an undeclared one.

## What Jelly does with it

Jelly applies the `access` setting itself, from the declared `readOnly` of each tool: at **Allowed** (the default) all
nine run without a prompt; at **Ask before changes** `boxd_status` and `boxd_job` run and the seven machine changes ask;
at **Read only** the two reads run and the seven changes are denied. A read-only helper is never given one of the seven
changes. The plugin's own guards that do not depend on a prompt hold in Jelly too: `boxd_drop` refuses a machine the
laptop cannot account for, and `boxd_sleep` always works.

# Live check on a real boxd machine

Everything in this file needs one real machine and your own boxd account. Nothing here runs in a check or a test: each
item is a place where the plugin's assumption is boxd's behaviour, and a fake has hidden any gap.

Run it once before the first release, and again after a boxd CLI or API change. Use a throwaway work id and snapshot,
and start from a clean ledger (`~/.local/share/opencode-boxd/works/` with no work you care about).

## 1. The argv the CLI actually accepts

- `boxd machine new <name> --from-snapshot <snapshot> --label role=session --label work=<id> --json` — label syntax, and
  the rules for a `work=` value.
- `boxd machine config set <name> auto-hibernate.timeout 1800`, and `… 14400`.
- `boxd machine config set <name> idle.ignore-outbound off`, and `… on`.
- `boxd machine hibernate <name> --json`, `boxd machine wake <name> --json`, `boxd machine remove <name> -y`.
- `boxd snapshots list --json`, `boxd snapshots save <machine> <name> --json`.
- `boxd machine cp - <name>:/tmp/opencode-boxd/guest.py` reads stdin.
- `boxd machine exec <name> -- python3 /tmp/opencode-boxd/guest.py` passes stdin through and returns stdout.
- `boxd machine exec <name> -- ls -1a /tmp` prints the listing, `.` and `..` included, and lists `opencode-boxd`
  while the helper is there.
- `boxd machine list --json` lists every machine of the account, with `name`.
- `boxd auth login` is how a user signs in; the plugin never runs it.
- `boxd --help` on the laptop CLI does not carry both `boxd inside a machine` and `from inside the VM`, the two phrases
  the in-VM CLI's help uses and `src/cli-flavor.ts` requires together. Only the in-VM help has been read; the laptop CLI's has not.

If any key or flag differs, the whole control plane is inert and the fakes hid it. Note the exact shape in
`docs/architecture.md` once confirmed.

## 2. The billing model

- Whether a hibernated machine bills.
- What `auto-hibernate.timeout` a new machine has before the plugin sets it, and whether `wake` resets it.
- Whether inbound `machine exec` traffic resets idleness once `idle.ignore-outbound` is `off`: that is the claim that a
  crashed laptop stops paying after 30 minutes.
- Whether `hibernate` and `stop` differ in billing and in what survives.

## 3. Provisioning time

Time `machine new` from the golden snapshot, against the 30 s timeout, and confirm whether a create that times out still
lands. Then check `boxd_status`: a machine that landed must appear as an orphan (or be adopted by `boxd_ensure`), never
be invisible.

## 4. The `machine get --json` vocabulary

Record the exact `status`/`boot`/`sharing`/`isolated` strings for running, starting, hibernating, suspended/standby,
destroyed and not-found. `src/cli-boxd.ts` maps them, and a wrong mapping lets a shared machine past `refuseUnsafe`.

## 5. The golden image

- Its OpenCode version, and whether it equals the laptop's (`boxd_status` shows the expected version).
- Whether `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096` accepts `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` from the guest helper.
- That port 4096 is not published, and nothing else listens on it.
- That `git`, `python3` and the in-VM `boxd` CLI exist, and that the machine is not created `--shared` or `--isolated`.

## 6. One full work, then the failure paths

1. `boxd_ensure` → `boxd_submit` → `boxd_job` → `boxd_harvest` → `boxd_sleep` → `boxd_resume` (wake).
2. Destroy the machine from the boxd CLI, then `boxd_resume` (rebuild from the golden snapshot and the transcript), then
   destroy and rebuild a second time in the same OpenCode run: the guest helper must be re-uploaded each time.
   Then reboot or resize the machine from the boxd CLI in the same run: the next `boxd_job` must copy the helper again
   (one `ls -1a /tmp` probe, one copy) and answer.
3. `boxd_image` from a machine with a fresh proof; then a machine whose image version differs from the laptop's (expect
   `GUEST_VERSION`, and `boxd_sleep` must still work).
4. Kill the guest OpenCode mid-run: `boxd_job`, `boxd_harvest` and `boxd_resume` must each give a coded error, and
   `boxd_sleep` must still hibernate.
5. A drop with an untracked file, with an ignored file, in a non-git directory, and with a staged change (expect
   `UNTRACKED`, `GIT_UNKNOWN`, or a stored patch and a successful drop).
6. `boxd_job` on a hibernated work: `asleep`, no wake, no billing.
7. After a wake, read `boxd machine get` and confirm `auto-hibernate.timeout` is 1800 and `idle.ignore-outbound` is off.

## 7. Concurrency

Two boxd tools in one `Promise.all` script (`boxd_submit` and `boxd_harvest`): the ledger must keep both, and the
harvest must record the proof as stale when the submit wins. Then two `boxd` CLI commands at once: note whether boxd
serialises them or refuses one.

# Scripting

Every boxd tool is a method of the `boxd.machines.tools` RPC, so a script calls it with no model, as a session and the
agent it names. A script's grant is a rule in config: only a resolved `allow` runs, an `ask` is refused because no one
can answer it, and a `deny` runs nothing.

The session is created for the script with an agent (`opencode api post /api/session -d '{"title":"…","agent":"build","location":{"directory":"/path/to/project"}}'`, with `data.id` kept). The body is
`{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{…}}}`; both keys are required, and no other key is allowed. Give the project as the session's `location`: a session made without one belongs to the service's default location, where the project's agents may not exist, and each call then fails `Agent not found`.

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/boxd.machines.tools/boxd_job -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{"workId":"review-api"}}}'
```

`describe` takes no input, or a session, and lists every method with its class and — given a session — the permission the
call would get:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/boxd.machines.tools/describe -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>"}}'
```

A plugin-owned method's result is the method's output object, as `describe` gives its schema: for boxd, the JSON the
tool itself returns (a work's state, a harvest's sessions, a job's outcome). `text` is what the model path would show.

## Methods

| Method | Class | Runs when |
|---|---|---|
| `boxd_status` | read | allowed |
| `boxd_job` | read | allowed |
| `boxd_ensure` | write | the agent or session allows `boxd_ensure` |
| `boxd_submit` | write | the agent or session allows `boxd_submit` |
| `boxd_harvest` | export | the agent or session allows `boxd_harvest` (it writes this laptop) |
| `boxd_sleep` | write | the agent or session allows `boxd_sleep` |
| `boxd_resume` | write | the agent or session allows `boxd_resume` |
| `boxd_image` | write | the agent or session allows `boxd_image` |
| `boxd_drop` | destructive | the agent or session allows `boxd_drop` |

A class is the worst thing the method does; it never decides whether a call runs. The rules do.

## Files in and out

`boxd_submit` takes `files` to copy data to the machine, and `boxd_harvest` takes `files` to copy results back. A path is
relative to the work tree; a laptop path must be inside the project or a folder in `allowedRoots`, and a symlink is never
followed. The caps are 8 MiB a file and 32 MiB a call, and the ledger records each file's name, size and sha256, never
its content.

A worked example: summarise the bookmarks a previous step saved, and bring the summary back.

```sh
# 1. One work, with the laptop folder it belongs to.
opencode api post /api/rpc/boxd.machines.tools/boxd_ensure -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" \
  -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{"workId":"bookmarks"}}}'

# 2. The data in, then the prompt. The model reads data/bookmarks.json, not a pasted list.
opencode api post /api/rpc/boxd.machines.tools/boxd_submit -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" \
  -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{"workId":"bookmarks","text":"Read data/bookmarks.json and write SUMMARY.md: one line per site, grouped by topic.","files":[{"from":"bookmarks.json","to":"data/bookmarks.json"}]}}}'

# 3. Later: the outcome, then the transcript and the summary.
opencode api post /api/rpc/boxd.machines.tools/boxd_job -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" \
  -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{"workId":"bookmarks"}}}'
opencode api post /api/rpc/boxd.machines.tools/boxd_harvest -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" \
  -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"<id>","input":{"workId":"bookmarks","files":["SUMMARY.md"]}}}'
```

The harvest answers `outcome: "completed"` when the model finished, and the file lands beside the work's laptop folder.
An `outcome` of `failed` is a warning on a successful harvest: the transcript and the files are still here, and the next
step says what to fix. A `boxd_drop` after that harvest succeeds, because `SUMMARY.md` came back at the digest the guest
still has; a file that was never harvested keeps the refusal.

If the host asks for permission to touch a folder outside the project, allow it with the `external_directory` rule as
well as the path rule:

```jsonc
{ "permissions": [
  { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "/srv/work/*", "effect": "allow" },
  { "action": "read", "resource": "/srv/work/**", "effect": "allow" },
  { "action": "edit", "resource": "/srv/work/**", "effect": "allow" }
] }
```

A refusal that names `permission.rejected: external_directory` is fixed by that rule, and by naming the folder in the
plugin's `allowedRoots` option.

## Restricting one agent

To let one agent run a script that harvests, give that agent its own rule:

```jsonc
{ "agents": { "harvester": { "permissions": [{ "action": "boxd_harvest", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" }] } } }
```

Every tool is allowed by default (the plugin's `access` option is `"all"`), and a script gets the same default: the
tools RPC resolves a rule before dispatch, and the default allow is that rule, so a script can call every method. To
restrict a script, set `access` to `"ask-changes"` (an `ask` is refused, because no one can answer it) or
`"read-only"`, or give the script's agent its own `deny` rule — the script's grant is a rule in config.

## The location

Run the command in the project whose agent you mean, and send the call to that location explicitly:

```sh
opencode api post /api/rpc/<id>/<method> -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{…}'
```

Without it the call goes to the service's default location and fails `rpc.unavailable` if the plugin is not loaded
there. The HTTP equivalents are the `location[directory]` query parameter and the same header. `describe` reports the
`location` that answered and a `locationHint`.

A location unloads after OpenCode's idle timeout. If a scheduled script gets `rpc.unavailable` from a location that was
loaded before, send the call again once: the request loads the location. Jobs keeps its own location loaded.

## Refusals

A call the RPC refuses before the method runs is the RPC error `failed`, with `data: { code, next }`:

| Code | When | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `PERMISSION_DENIED` | the rule resolves to ask, or a deny hides the method | add an allow rule for the action to the session's agent or to the session |
| `SESSION_UNKNOWN` | OpenCode does not know the session in this location | create the session in the location you mean, and pass its id |
| `SESSION_AGENT_REQUIRED` | the session names no agent | create a session that names an agent |
| `TOOL_UNAVAILABLE` | OpenCode does not list the method's tool now | call `describe` to see the methods there are |

A method that ran and refused answers with its output, not an RPC error: `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<what
happened>", "next": "<the one next step>" }`, the same object the model path gets. The codes a script meets most:

| Code | When | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `NOT_OURS` | no open work has that id, or it is bound to another machine | call `boxd_ensure` for that work id |
| `MACHINE_GONE` | the machine is missing or destroyed | call `boxd_resume` to rebuild it from the golden snapshot |
| `SNAPSHOT_MISSING` | the golden snapshot is not in this boxd account | build the image as `docs/golden-image.md` describes, and set `snapshot` |
| `SESSION_BUSY` | the guest session is still running | call `boxd_job` until it reports idle, then harvest |
| `NOT_PROVEN` | no fresh laptop import since the last prompt | call `boxd_harvest` first |
| `GUEST_RUN_FAILED`, `GUEST_AUTH_FAILED` | the guest session's last run failed | read the transcript, then `boxd_submit` again; an auth failure is fixed in the image |
| `RUN_INTERRUPTED` | `boxd_resume` only: the guest's OpenCode stopped during the session's run | harvest what exists with `boxd_harvest`, then `boxd_submit` again |

Every other code the plugin raises is in `docs/configuration.md`, with its one next step.

Known limit: a saved "Always allow" answer from an earlier session is not part of the agent and session rules, so it
does not authorize an ad hoc script. A script's grant is a rule in config.
